working_title: County Down's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is home to what Golf Digest ranks as the world's number one course, yet most UK visitors treat it as a one-club pilgrimage rather than a proper golf circuit. The post makes the case for spending several days exploring three distinct links, each with its own character and price point, and gives the practical logistics a UK visitor actually needs.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle, Co Down: founded 1889, shaped from natural duneland, two 18-hole courses (Championship Links and Annesley Links). Championship sits between the Mourne Mountains and Dundrum Bay. Golf Digest ranked it #1 in the world on its 2024 World's 100 Greatest Courses list. Par 71, slope 142 from blue tees. No buggies permitted.
- RCD visitor access (per multiple sources, 2026): Mon, Tue, Fri (all day); Thu (morning only); Sun (afternoon only). Wednesdays and Saturdays closed to visitors. Advance booking essential; club operates a waitlist system. Championship green fee listed by Wandering Golfers as £450 for 2026; Golfshake shows midweek £110–£125 (possibly Annesley). Treat Championship fee as 'premium/seasonal – check royalcountydown.org for current rates'. Annesley Links considerably cheaper.
- RCD has hosted the Walker Cup, multiple Irish Opens and Senior British Opens.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole cliffside links, par 70, 5,814 yards, Castle Place, Ardglass, BT30 7TP. Founded 1896 by Rev Thomas MacAfee. Clubhouse is reputedly the oldest building used as a golf clubhouse in the world – a fortified warehouse/castle dating to no later than 1405. First five holes run along cliffs above the Irish Sea. Ranked in Irish Golfer's top 50 Irish courses 2026. High-season visitor green fee (2026, per official site): £250 for 18 holes / £375 daily; shoulder (April) £125; low season (Nov, Feb–Mar) £90. Golf Ireland member rates lower. Visitors available most days outside member-reserved Saturday morning and Sunday morning blocks. Days to avoid: Wednesdays and busy weekends.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: Cloughey, Ards Peninsula, Co Down, BT22 1JA. Founded 1902, designed by James Braid (visited 1934). 18-hole links, par 69/70, 6,167 yards. Most easterly 18-hole course on island of Ireland; nearest links to Belfast (approx 45 min by road). Lowest rainfall area of Northern Ireland; free-draining sandy base – good year-round conditions. Signature hole: par-4 10th (435 yards, one of the hardest par 4s in Irish golf). Open to visitors every day; advance booking advised. Green fees modest compared to RCD/Ardglass – multiple sources cite approximately £40/round (verify directly with club as this may be outdated).
- Getting there from mainland UK: Fly to Belfast City Airport (closest to County Down) or Belfast International. Ferry options: Cairnryan (Scotland) to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 2h15; Cairnryan to Larne with P&O, approx 2h; Liverpool Birkenhead to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 8h (overnight option available). Car recommended for getting around County Down.
- Newcastle (RCD base): Slieve Donard Resort (4-star) is immediately adjacent to RCD first tee; Burrendale Hotel about one mile from RCD gates.
- Ardglass is roughly 20 miles up the coast from RCD (Newcastle). Kirkistown is on the Ards Peninsula, approx 45 min from Belfast by road.
- Warrenpoint Golf Club (parkland, 1893) and Clandeboye Golf Club (36-hole parkland, Conlig) are additional County Down options for mixed-format trips.
- Note on prices: Ardglass official 2026 green fees are confirmed from club's own site. RCD Championship fees vary by source; do not state a specific figure – direct reader to club website. Kirkistown fees should be confirmed directly with the club.
